To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the clinical usefulness of the MMP-2, -9, TIMP1 and TIMP2 levels of synthesis has been investigated in non-small cell cancer (NSCL).
the evaluation of gelatinases levels of synthesis in non-small cell cancer could be useful for selecting patients with unfavourable clinical outcome, in order to establish adequate adjuvant therapy.
the levels of synthesis of MMP-2 and TIMP- 1 are associated with the clinical outcome of NSCLC patients, and that the levels of MMP-9 are related with the clinical evolution of NSCLC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new prognostic markers in NSCLC, which could be of clinical utility to establish adjuvante therapies.
the study of the clinical and prognostic significance of the expression of MMP-2 and MMP-9 and their inhibitors TIMP-1, TIMP-2.
the identification of new prognostic factors in NSCLC, which could be used for the establishment of adjuvant therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MMP-9 levels and TIMP- 1 levels are useful parameters in the clinical management of NSCLC.
the MMP-2, TIMP-2 and MMP-9 levels of synthesis and the TIMP-1 net activity, are useful for the clinical follow up of NSCLC patients.
MMP-2 and TIMP-3 levels are not useful for the clinical management of NSCLC, whereas MMP-9 and, especially, TIMP-3 are of potential clinical value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evaluation of gelatinases levels and their tissue inhibitors could be a good tool for the prediction of clinical evolution of NSCLC patients.
MMP-2, TIMP-2 and TIMP-3 levels of synthesis do not have prognostic value.

the evaluation of the levels of gelatinases (MMPs) and their inhibitors (TIMPs) in tumours could be useful to select patients with potentially unfavoured clinical evolution in order establish adjuvant therapies protocols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of MMP and TIMP levels of synthesis could help in the clinical management of NSCLC patients.
the evaluation of gelatinases activity and their tissue inhibitors could help to establish adjuvancy protocols and to predict the clinical evolution of patients.
the levels of MMP-9 and especially of TIMP-1 can be used for the selection of high risk patients with NSCLC in order to establish more aggressive therapeutic protocols.
